name: TIMES
aliases: Tolterodine and Tamsulosin in Men With LUTS Including OAB
question: Does tolterodine extended release plus tamsulosin improve perceived benefit and storage symptoms in men with LUTS and OAB compared with either drug alone or placebo?

design.population: Men aged at least 40 years with moderate-to-severe LUTS, bothersome bladder symptoms, and diary-documented frequency and urgency, with or without urgency urinary incontinence.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, four-arm superiority randomized trial
design.locator: JAMA article, Methods: Patients and Study Design; Results: Patient Disposition

verdictNote: Combination beat placebo on perceived benefit; the trial lasted 12 weeks.
takeaway: In men with LUTS and OAB, tolterodine ER plus tamsulosin improved week-12 patient-perceived benefit versus placebo; neither tolterodine ER nor tamsulosin alone significantly improved that primary outcome versus placebo after correction of a reported P value.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Kaplan SA, Roehrborn CG, Rovner ES, et al. "Tolterodine and tamsulosin for treatment of men with lower urinary tract symptoms and overactive bladder: a randomized controlled trial." *JAMA.* 2006;296(19):2319-2328. doi:10.1001/jama.296.19.2319

results.measure: Week-12 benefit among participants with an available response; risk difference for combination versus placebo, percentage points
results.note: Protocol-specified ITT population: combination n=217, tolterodine ER n=210, tamsulosin n=209, placebo n=215; 2, 1, 2, and 1, respectively, had no available benefit response. Missing postbaseline responses were imputed by last observation carried forward. Corrected tamsulosin-placebo P=0.064; tolterodine-placebo P=0.48.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Efficacy End Points, pp 2323–2324; 2007 correction, p 1864

results.endpoint: Patient-perceived treatment benefit, missing counted as no benefit
results.measure: Post hoc week-12 analysis using randomized arm denominators; risk difference for combination versus placebo, percentage points
results.note: Post hoc sensitivity analysis; no prespecified success threshold. Table 2 rounds the exact confidence interval to whole percentage points.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, post hoc intention-to-treat analysis, p 2324

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in episodes per 24 hours at week 12
results.note: Analyzed only among men with urgency urinary incontinence at baseline. Baseline UUI subset: combination n=52, placebo n=48; week-12 observed diary counts 47 and 43. Adjusted means used ITT imputation.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Figure 2A, pp 2323, 2325

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in episodes per 24 hours at week 12
results.locator: Full text, Figure 2B and abstract, pp 2319, 2325
results.note: Week-12 observed diary counts: combination n=211, placebo n=210; adjusted means used ITT imputation.

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in micturitions per 24 hours at week 12
results.locator: Full text, Figure 2C and abstract, pp 2319, 2325
results.note: Week-12 observed diary counts: combination n=211, placebo n=212; adjusted means used ITT imputation.

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in micturitions per night at week 12
results.locator: Full text, Figure 2D and abstract, pp 2319, 2325
results.note: Week-12 observed diary counts: combination n=209, placebo n=212; adjusted means used ITT imputation.

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in total IPSS at week 12
results.locator: Full text, Figure 3A and abstract, pp 2319, 2326
results.note: Week-12 observed IPSS counts: combination n=203, placebo n=213; adjusted means used ITT imputation.

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in IPSS quality-of-life item at week 12
results.note: Week-12 observed IPSS QOL counts: combination n=205, placebo n=213; adjusted means used ITT imputation. No prespecified confirmatory threshold for this secondary endpoint.
results.locator: Full text, abstract and Figure 3B, pp 2319, 2326

delivery.label: Daily drug regimen
delivery.value: Tolterodine ER 4 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, both, or matched placebo once daily for 12 weeks, about 30 minutes after dinner.

delivery.label: Medication adherence
delivery.value: More than 95% of the intention-to-treat population in each group ingested at least 80% of assigned medication.

reports.label: Tamsulosin P-value correction
reports.citation: "Incorrect Data in: Tolterodine and Tamsulosin for Treatment of Men With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Overactive Bladder: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *JAMA.* 2007;298(16):1864. doi:10.1001/jama.298.16.1864
reports.followUp: Correction to the primary report; no new follow-up

reports.label: PSA subgroup analysis
reports.citation: Roehrborn CG, Kaplan SA, Kraus SR, et al. "Effects of serum PSA on efficacy of tolterodine extended release with or without tamsulosin in men with LUTS, including OAB." *Urology.* 2008;72(5):1061-1067. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2008.06.067
reports.followUp: Post hoc analysis of the original 12-week trial
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Subjects and Study Design, p 1062

results.measure: Least squares mean change in micturitions per 24 hours at week 12; baseline PSA at least 1.3 versus below 1.3 ng/mL
results.note: Post hoc comparisons with placebo: combination P<0.001 at PSA ≥1.3; tolterodine ER and combination each P=0.010 at PSA <1.3. No confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Bladder Diary Variables, pp 1062–1064

results.measure: Least squares mean change in summed urgency ratings per 24 hours at week 12; PSA at least 1.3 versus below 1.3 ng/mL
results.note: Post hoc comparisons with placebo: combination P=0.006 at PSA ≥1.3; tolterodine ER P=0.011 and combination P=0.009 at PSA <1.3. No confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Bladder Diary Variables, pp 1063–1064

results.endpoint: IPSS storage score by baseline PSA
results.measure: Least squares mean change in IPSS storage score at week 12; PSA at least 1.3 versus below 1.3 ng/mL
results.note: Post hoc comparisons with placebo: combination P=0.001 at PSA ≥1.3; tolterodine ER P=0.033 and combination P=0.018 at PSA <1.3. No confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and International Prostate Symptom Score, pp 1063–1064

results.measure: Least squares mean change in total IPSS at week 12; PSA at least 1.3 versus below 1.3 ng/mL
results.note: Post hoc comparisons with placebo at PSA ≥1.3: tamsulosin P=0.007 and combination P=0.007; none significant at PSA <1.3. No confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and International Prostate Symptom Score, pp 1063–1064

results.endpoint: IPSS voiding score by baseline PSA
results.measure: Least squares mean change in IPSS voiding score at week 12; PSA at least 1.3 versus below 1.3 ng/mL
results.note: Post hoc comparisons with placebo: tamsulosin P=0.005 at PSA ≥1.3; none significant at PSA <1.3. No confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and International Prostate Symptom Score, pp 1064–1065

harms.label: Urinary retention by baseline PSA

values.exp: One PSA ≥1.3 recipient discontinued because of acute urinary retention; other diagnoses by arm not specified
values.tol: One PSA ≥1.3 recipient discontinued because of acute urinary retention; other diagnoses by arm not specified

harms.note: Four men with PSA ≥1.3 ng/mL were diagnosed with urinary retention; none with PSA <1.3 ng/mL. Safety denominators by stratum were not reported. No significant changes in postvoid residual volume or maximum flow rate were found in any group.
harms.locator: Full text, abstract p 1061 and Safety p 1065
